## SaveSystem

`core/save_system.gd` · extends `RefCounted`

JSON save slots under `user://saves/`, stamped with a schema version so old files can be detected instead of crashing a load.

```gdscript
SaveSystem.store("progress", {"level": 3, "best": 1200})
var data := SaveSystem.fetch("progress", {"level": 1, "best": 0})
```

### Constants

- `const DIR := "user://saves"`
- `const VERSION := 1` — Bumped when the envelope format changes. Slots written by a newer version are refused rather than misread.

### Methods

- `static func path_for(slot: String) -> String` — Absolute `user://` path of a slot's file.
- `static func sanitize(slot: String) -> String` — Lower-cases a slot name and strips anything that is not a safe filename character.
- `static func store(slot: String, data: Dictionary) -> Error` — Writes `data` to a slot. Returns `OK` or the file error.
- `static func fetch(slot: String, fallback: Dictionary = {}) -> Dictionary` — Reads a slot. Returns `fallback` when the slot is missing, unreadable, malformed, or written by a newer `VERSION`.
- `static func has_slot(slot: String) -> bool`
- `static func erase(slot: String) -> Error` — Deletes a slot. Returns `OK` when the slot is gone afterwards.
- `static func slots() -> PackedStringArray` — Slot names currently on disk, sorted.

## Session

`core/session.gd` · extends `Node`

The round lifecycle shared by every GodotGo game: a small state machine with a score, an objective counter and an optional countdown.

A game adds a subclass as an autoload named `Game`:

```gdscript
# scripts/game.gd, registered in project.godot as Game="*res://scripts/game.gd"
extends Session
```

Scenes call `start()`, `advance()`, `add_score()`, `win()` and `lose()`, and react to the signals. No rule here needs a node reference, so every rule stays unit-testable headlessly.

### Signals

- `signal state_changed(state: State)` — Emitted when `state` changes. Never emitted for a same-state assignment.
- `signal score_changed(score: int)` — Emitted after `start()` and every successful `add_score()`.
- `signal progress_changed(progress: int, goal: int)` — Emitted after `start()` and every successful `advance()`.
- `signal time_changed(time_left: float)` — Emitted after `start()` and whenever the countdown's tenths digit changes.
- `signal objective_reached` — Emitted exactly once per round, the moment `progress` reaches `goal`.
- `signal won(result: Dictionary)` — Emitted by `win()` with the round summary from `summary()`.
- `signal lost(reason: String)` — Emitted by `lose()` with one of the REASON constants or a game-specific string.

### Enums

- `enum State { READY, PLAYING, PAUSED, WON, LOST }`

### Constants

- `const REASON_TIME := "time"` — The countdown reached zero.
- `const REASON_DEATH := "death"` — The player died.
- `const REASON_QUIT := "quit"` — The player gave up or left the round.
- `const LOG_PREFIX := "[godotgo]"` — Prefix for the framework's stdout lines; `tools/smoke.sh` looks for it.

### Properties

- `var state: State = State.READY`
- `var score := 0`
- `var progress := 0` — Objective units completed so far (orbs collected, boxes placed, waves survived).
- `var goal := 0` — Objective units needed to finish. 0 means the round has no counted objective.
- `var time_limit := 0.0` — Seconds allowed for the round. 0 disables the countdown.
- `var time_left := 0.0`
- `var elapsed := 0.0` — Seconds spent in `State.PLAYING` this round.

### Methods

- `func start(goal_value: int = 0, limit: float = 0.0) -> void` — Begins a round. `goal_value` of 0 means no counted objective; `limit` of 0 means no countdown.
- `func add_score(points: int) -> bool` — Adds points. Returns false (and changes nothing) unless a round is running.
- `func advance(amount: int = 1) -> bool` — Advances the objective counter, emitting `objective_reached` the first time `progress` reaches `goal`. Returns false unless playing.
- `func objective_complete() -> bool` — True once `progress` has reached a non-zero `goal`.
- `func is_playing() -> bool`
- `func is_over() -> bool`
- `func tick(delta: float) -> void` — Advances the clock. Called every frame by `_process()`; call it directly in tests to step time deterministically.
- `func pause() -> bool` — Suspends the clock without ending the round.
- `func resume() -> bool`
- `func win() -> bool` — Ends the round as a win. Ignored unless playing.
- `func lose(reason: String = REASON_QUIT) -> bool` — Ends the round as a loss. Ignored unless playing.
- `func summary() -> Dictionary` — A snapshot of the round, used by `won` and by save files.
- `func reset() -> void` — Returns to `State.READY` with every counter cleared.

## GodotGoMcpBridge

`mcp/mcp_bridge.gd` · extends `RefCounted` · `@tool`

Publishes GodotGo's own tools to an MCP agent through the Godot AI addon.

Godot AI (github.com/hi-godot/godot-ai) gives an agent about 120 tools for driving a live editor: nodes, scenes, scripts, animation, materials. What it cannot know is this workspace — that a round lives in a [`Session`](#session) subclass, that a project is verified by `tools/verify.sh`, that an empty test suite is a failure rather than a pass. This registers that knowledge as additional tools, so one agent can both build a scene and prove it still works.

Godot AI is an optional dependency. Nothing here references its classes by name: the scripts are loaded by path and duck-typed, so the framework parses and runs identically on a machine that has never installed it. That is why the handler signatures below leave `ctx` untyped — naming `McpCallContext` would make this file fail to parse without it.

```gdscript
var bridge := GodotGoMcpBridge.new()
bridge.register_tools()   # 0 when Godot AI is absent, never an error
```

### Constants

- `const REGISTRY_SCRIPT := "res://addons/godot_ai/custom_tools/mcp_tool_registry.gd"` — Where the vendored addon puts the pieces we duck-type against.
- `const SPEC_SCRIPT := "res://addons/godot_ai/custom_tools/mcp_custom_tool_spec.gd"`
- `const SOURCE_PATH := "res://addons/godotgo/plugin.cfg"` — Identifies these tools as ours in Godot AI's dock and collision policy.
- `const SOURCE_NAME := "godotgo"`
- `const HANDLERS_SCRIPT := "res://addons/godotgo/mcp/mcp_handlers.gd"` — The handlers live in a separate script because the registry materialises them lazily by path, so a hot reload cannot free an instance mid-call.
- `const MAX_TIMEOUT_MS := 120000` — Ceiling Godot AI enforces on a deferred tool. A whole-workspace verify runs longer than this, which is why every tool that shells out takes one project.

### Methods

- `static func is_available() -> bool` — True when the Godot AI addon is installed and its registry is live. Both halves matter: the scripts can be present while the plugin is disabled.
- `func register_tools() -> int` — Registers every GodotGo tool, replacing any previous registration of the same names. Returns how many were accepted; 0 means Godot AI is not available, which is a normal state and not an error.
- `func unregister_tools() -> void` — Removes the tools again, for when the framework plugin is disabled while Godot AI stays up.
- `static func build_specs(spec_script: Resource) -> Array` — Turns the definitions into Godot AI spec objects. Separate from registration so the framework's tests can hand them to Godot AI's own validator, which is a far better check of the budgets than a copy of its constants.

## mcp/mcp_handlers.gd

extends `RefCounted` · `@tool`

Implements the tools [`GodotGoMcpBridge`](#godotgomcpbridge) publishes to an MCP agent.

Every method here has the signature Godot AI's dispatcher calls, `(params: Dictionary, ctx) -> Dictionary`, and returns either `{"data": ...}` or `{"status": "error", "error": ...}`. `ctx` is deliberately untyped: naming Godot AI's class would stop this file parsing on a machine that has not installed it, and the framework must load the same everywhere. See [`GodotGoMcpBridge`](#godotgomcpbridge) for the whole rationale.

The shell-outs run on a worker thread and answer through `ctx.send_deferred()`, because a synchronous `OS.execute()` would freeze the editor for the minute a verify takes.

### Constants

- `const DEFERRED := {"_deferred": true}` — Godot AI's marker for "the answer is coming later".

### Methods

- `func verify(params: Dictionary, ctx) -> Dictionary`
- `func check(params: Dictionary, ctx) -> Dictionary`
- `func test(params: Dictionary, ctx) -> Dictionary`
- `func projects(_params: Dictionary, _ctx) -> Dictionary`
- `func framework_api(params: Dictionary, _ctx) -> Dictionary`

## GodotGoTest

`testing/test_case.gd` · extends `RefCounted`

Base class for headless unit tests, shared by every project in the workspace. Subclass in a project's tests/unit/test_\*.gd and add methods prefixed with test_. Methods may use await (e.g. on tree.physics_frame) and the runner will wait for them.

### Properties

- `var tree: SceneTree` — The running SceneTree, for tests that need to add nodes or await frames.

### Methods

- `func before_each() -> void` — Called before every test_ method.
- `func after_each() -> void` — Called after every test_ method, even when it failed.
- `func fail(message: String) -> void`
- `func skip(reason: String) -> void` — Marks the current test as skipped. Remaining assertions still run but the runner reports the test as skipped rather than passed or failed.
- `func is_headless() -> bool` — True when running without a real display (CI, tools/test.sh).
- `func assert_true(condition: bool, message: String = "") -> void`
- `func assert_false(condition: bool, message: String = "") -> void`
- `func assert_eq(actual: Variant, expected: Variant, message: String = "") -> void`
- `func assert_ne(actual: Variant, unexpected: Variant, message: String = "") -> void`
- `func assert_almost_eq(actual: float, expected: float, tolerance: float = 0.0001, message: String = "") -> void`
- `func assert_null(value: Variant, message: String = "") -> void`
- `func assert_not_null(value: Variant, message: String = "") -> void`
- `func assert_is(value: Variant, type: Variant, message: String = "") -> void`
- `func add_scene(scene: PackedScene) -> Node` — Instantiates a PackedScene, adds it to the tree root, and returns it. Free it with `free_node()` in `after_each()`.
- `func add_node(node: Node) -> Node` — Adds an existing node to the tree root.
- `func free_node(node: Variant) -> void` — Queues a node for deletion and waits until it is gone. Accepts an already freed reference (e.g. a node that freed itself) without complaint.
- `func physics_frames(count: int) -> void` — Waits for `count` physics frames. Resumes inside the physics frame, before nodes process, so Input.action_press calls made right after are seen as "just pressed" by _physics_process in that same frame.
- `func record(sig: Signal) -> Array` — Records every emission of `sig` until the test ends. Each entry is the emitted arguments padded with nulls to three items; use size() for counts.
- `func add_floor_3d() -> StaticBody3D` — Adds a 40 x 1 x 40 static 3D floor on physics layer 1 whose top surface is y = 0.
- `func add_floor_2d() -> StaticBody2D` — Adds a 2000 x 40 static 2D floor on physics layer 1 whose top edge is y = 0.

## testing/test_runner.gd

extends `SceneTree`

Zero-dependency headless test runner.

Usage:

```text
tools/godot.sh --headless --path . --script res://tests/test_runner.gd
tools/godot.sh --headless --path . --script res://tests/test_runner.gd -- --filter=player
```

Discovers tests/unit/\*\*/test_\*.gd, instantiates each (must extend GodotGoTest), runs every test_\* method, prints a summary, and exits 1 on any failure.

### Constants

- `const TEST_ROOT := "res://tests/unit"`

## tools/check_scripts.gd

extends `SceneTree`

Loads scripts, scenes and resources to validate them, then exits 1 if any failed. Unlike `godot --check-only` this runs inside a live SceneTree, so autoload singletons resolve, `class_name` lookups work and .tscn/.tres files are validated as well. It is also the only form that reports failure on macOS, where --check-only always exits 0.

Usage:

```text
godot --headless --path <project> --script res://addons/godotgo/tools/check_scripts.gd
godot --headless --path <project> --script res://addons/godotgo/tools/check_scripts.gd \
    -- scripts/level.gd scenes/main.tscn
```

With no file arguments it scans the whole project, skipping SKIPPED_DIRS. Callers that want the shared addon checked (the framework project does) pass files explicitly; tools/check.sh always does.

### Constants

- `const SKIPPED_DIRS: Array[String] = [".godot", ".git", "addons"]`
- `const CHECKED_EXTENSIONS: Array[String] = ["gd", "tscn", "tres"]`

## tools/new_uid.gd

extends `SceneTree`

Prints a fresh Godot resource UID for use in hand-written .tscn/.tres files. Usage: tools/godot.sh --headless --path . --script res://scripts/tools/new_uid.gd

## MaterialMakerLoader

`util/material_maker_loader.gd` · extends `RefCounted`

Loads a Material Maker Godot export (StandardMaterial3D .tres) or builds one from PBR maps sitting next to the material.

Usage:

```gdscript
var mat := MaterialMakerLoader.load_material("res://materials/rust", "rust")
$MeshInstance3D.material_override = mat
```

### Constants

- `const MAP_CANDIDATES: Dictionary[String, Array] = {…}` — StandardMaterial3D texture property -> candidate file names, tried in order. "%s" is replaced with the material stem (the .tres name without extension).
- `const ORM_CANDIDATES: Array = ["%s_orm.png", "orm.png"]` — Packed occlusion/roughness/metallic map as written by Material Maker's "Godot 4 Standard" export. Used when the separate maps are absent.
- `const ORM_CHANNELS: Dictionary[String, BaseMaterial3D.TextureChannel] = {…}` — ORM channel layout (glTF convention): R = ambient occlusion, G = roughness, B = metallic.
- `const FEATURE_FLAGS: Dictionary[String, String] = {…}` — Texture properties whose feature toggle must be switched on for the map to render.

### Methods

- `static func load_material(material_dir: String, material_name: String = "") -> StandardMaterial3D` — Returns the exported .tres at `material_dir/material_name.tres` when it exists, otherwise a StandardMaterial3D assembled from whichever PBR maps are present. `material_name` defaults to the directory name.
- `static func find_maps(material_dir: String, stem: String) -> Dictionary[String, String]` — Lists which maps `load_material()` would pick up for a material, keyed by StandardMaterial3D property. A packed ORM map is reported under the key "orm". Useful for tooling and tests.

## ObjectPool

`util/object_pool.gd` · extends `Node`

Reuses instances of a `PackedScene` instead of allocating one per spawn.

Spare instances are held outside the scene tree; `acquire()` hands one back for the caller to add wherever it likes, and `release()` takes it out of the tree and returns it to the pool.

```gdscript
var bullet := pool.acquire()
if bullet:
    add_child(bullet)
    bullet.global_position = muzzle.global_position
# later
pool.release(bullet)
```

A pooled scene may implement `pool_acquired()` and `pool_released()` to reset its own state; the pool calls them when they exist.

### Signals

- `signal acquired(node: Node)`
- `signal released(node: Node)`

### Properties

- `@export var scene: PackedScene` — The scene instantiated for every pooled object.
- `@export_range(0, 512, 1) var initial_size := 0` — Instances created up front in `_ready()`.
- `@export_range(0, 4096, 1) var max_size := 0` — Refuse to create more than this many live instances. 0 means no ceiling.

### Methods

- `func prewarm(count: int) -> void` — Creates instances ahead of time so the first spawns do not allocate.
- `func acquire() -> Node` — Returns a ready instance that is not in the tree, or null when `scene` is unset or `max_size` is reached.
- `func release(node: Node) -> void` — Removes `node` from the tree and returns it to the pool. Releasing a node twice, or one from another pool, is reported and ignored.
- `func release_all() -> void` — Releases everything currently handed out.
- `func in_use() -> int` — Instances currently handed out.
- `func available() -> int` — Spare instances ready to hand out.
- `func created() -> int` — Instances this pool has ever created.

## Rng

`util/rng.gd` · extends `RefCounted`

Deterministic random numbers. The same seed always produces the same sequence, which is what makes spawn patterns and shuffles testable.

```gdscript
var rng := Rng.new(1234)
var wave := rng.pick(["bat", "slime", "ghost"])
```

### Properties

- `var seed_value: int = 0` — The seed this generator was created or reseeded with.

### Methods

- `Rng.new(initial_seed: int = 0)`
- `func reseed(new_seed: int) -> void` — Restarts the sequence from `new_seed`.
- `func get_state() -> int` — Opaque generator position. Save it and assign it back to resume a sequence.
- `func set_state(value: int) -> void`
- `func randi() -> int`
- `func randi_range(from: int, to: int) -> int` — Inclusive on both ends.
- `func randf() -> float`
- `func randf_range(from: float, to: float) -> float`
- `func chance(probability: float) -> bool` — True with probability `probability` (0.0 never, 1.0 always).
- `func pick(items: Array) -> Variant` — A uniformly chosen element, or null for an empty array.
- `func shuffled(items: Array) -> Array` — A new array with the elements shuffled; the input is left alone.
- `func weighted_pick(items: Array, weights: Array) -> Variant` — Picks an element whose chance is proportional to its weight. Non-positive weights are ignored; returns null when nothing is selectable.
- `func point_in_rect(rect: Rect2) -> Vector2` — A random point inside the given rectangle.
- `func direction() -> Vector2` — A unit vector with a uniformly random direction.

## StateMachine

`util/state_machine.gd` · extends `RefCounted`

A small finite state machine for entity behaviour, built from callables so it needs no node hierarchy and can be unit-tested on its own.

```gdscript
var fsm := StateMachine.new()
fsm.add_state(&"idle", _idle_update)
fsm.add_state(&"chase", _chase_update, _on_chase_enter)
fsm.start(&"idle")
# in _physics_process:
fsm.update(delta)
```

### Signals

- `signal transitioned(from: StringName, to: StringName)` — Emitted on every accepted transition, including the initial `start()`.

### Properties

- `var current: StringName = &""`
- `var previous: StringName = &""`
- `var time_in_state := 0.0` — Seconds spent in `current`, reset on every transition.

### Methods

- `func add_state(state_name: StringName, on_update := Callable(), on_enter := Callable(), on_exit := Callable()) -> void` — Registers a state. Every callback is optional; `on_update` receives the frame delta, the others take no arguments.
- `func has_state(state_name: StringName) -> bool`
- `func states() -> Array[StringName]` — Registered state names, in alphabetical order.
- `func start(state_name: StringName) -> bool` — Enters the first state without running an exit callback. Returns false when the state is unknown.
- `func transition_to(state_name: StringName) -> bool` — Leaves the current state and enters `state_name`. Returns false when the state is unknown or already current.
- `func update(delta: float) -> void` — Runs the current state's update callback and advances `time_in_state`.

## TextGrid

`util/text_grid.gd` · extends `RefCounted`

An ASCII level map parsed into single-character cells.

Levels are plain text files, which makes them diffable, hand-editable and trivial to assert on in tests. Rows are padded with spaces to a common width.

```gdscript
var grid := TextGrid.parse("###\n#@#\n###")
grid.find_first("@")  # -> Vector2i(1, 1)
```

### Constants

- `const EMPTY := " "`

### Properties

- `var width := 0`
- `var height := 0`

### Methods

- `static func parse(text: String) -> TextGrid` — Parses text into a grid. Blank leading and trailing lines are dropped.
- `static func from_file(path: String) -> TextGrid` — Parses a `res://` or `user://` text file. Returns an empty grid when the file cannot be read.
- `func in_bounds(pos: Vector2i) -> bool`
- `func at(pos: Vector2i) -> String` — The character at `pos`, or `EMPTY` when out of bounds.
- `func cell(x: int, y: int) -> String`
- `func set_at(pos: Vector2i, symbol: String) -> void` — Overwrites one cell. Out-of-bounds writes are ignored.
- `func find_all(symbol: String) -> Array[Vector2i]` — Every position holding `symbol`, in reading order.
- `func find_first(symbol: String) -> Vector2i` — The first position holding `symbol`, or (-1, -1) when absent.
- `func find_any(symbols: String) -> Array[Vector2i]` — Every position whose character appears in `symbols`.
- `func count(symbol: String) -> int`
- `func clone() -> TextGrid` — An independent copy, safe to mutate.
- `func to_text() -> String`
